facts.text: The Egerton is a red-brick Victorian townhouse dating from 1843.
facts.excerpt: The Egerton, a red-brick Victorian townhouse dating from 1843, sits in the heart of Knightsbridge near Harrods, the Science Museum, and the Victoria & Albert Museum.

facts.text: The hotel is in the heart of Knightsbridge near Harrods, the Science Museum and the Victoria & Albert Museum.
facts.excerpt: sits in the heart of Knightsbridge near Harrods, the Science Museum, and the Victoria & Albert Museum

facts.text: The hotel is on a tranquil, leafy residential street.
facts.excerpt: Nestled on a tranquil, leafy residential street, our boutique hotel feels more like a cosy private residence.

facts.text: Through a long-standing partnership with the Victoria and Albert Museum, the hotel offers guests complimentary tickets to the V&A's feature exhibitions.
facts.excerpt: Through this exclusive relationship, we offer complimentary tickets to the V&A’s feature exhibitions, available exclusively for our guests.

facts.text: A limited number of V&A VIP access cards are available at reception each day.
facts.excerpt: Each day, a limited number of VIP access cards are available at reception, offering a truly elevated museum experience.

facts.text: V&A VIP cards include access to the V&A Members' Lounge.
facts.excerpt: Access to the V&A Members’ Lounge, a calm and elegant space to relax

facts.text: V&A VIP cards give entry to all temporary exhibitions, including sold-out ones.
facts.excerpt: Entry to all temporary exhibitions, including those that are sold out

facts.text: The hotel's top suite is the V&A Suite, named for its partnership with the Victoria and Albert Museum.
facts.excerpt: Our best suite, aptly named the V&A Suite, celebrates our treasured partnership with the Victoria and Albert Museum.

facts.text: The hotel displays original works of art by artists including Toulouse-Lautrec, Erte, Ludwig Bemelmans, Peanuts creator Charles M. Schulz, British cartoonist JAK and French caricaturist Sem.
facts.excerpt: original works of art by artists such as Toulouse-Lautrec, Erte, Ludwig Bemelmans, ‘Peanuts’ cartoon creator Charles M. Schulz, British cartoonist JAK and French caricaturist Sem

facts.text: Rooms have Savoir beds, luxury toiletries and plush bathrobes and slippers.
facts.excerpt:
- Luxury toiletries
- Sumptuous Savoir bed
- Plush bathrobes and slippers

facts.text: Some Deluxe King rooms have full-height bay windows that catch the afternoon sunlight.
facts.excerpt: A statement of style and opulence, some enjoying full-height bay windows that catch the afternoon sunlight.

facts.text: Interleading rooms can accommodate four to five people, depending on availability, and must be booked directly through the reservations team.
facts.excerpt: These rooms can accommodate four to five people, depending on availability, and must be booked directly through our reservations team.

facts.text: The bar serves the hotel's signature martini.
facts.excerpt: Relax in our elegant bar and sample a choice of expertly-mixed cocktails accompanied by homemade bites, including our signature Martini - known as one of London's best.

facts.text: Traditional afternoon tea is served in the Tea Room with loose-leaf tea and homemade treats.
facts.excerpt: Settle into our beautiful Tea Room with a fragrant pot of loose-leaf tea, or perhaps a glass of champagne, and prepare to be spoiled with a selection of homemade treats.

facts.text: Breakfast is served in the Dining Room or in your bedroom.
facts.excerpt: Begin your day in the right way, with a delicious breakfast served in either the Dining Room or your bedroom.

facts.text: The hotel offers a Pawtrait Experience for guests' dogs with resident artist Shelly Levy.
facts.excerpt: Treat your pup to a Pawtrait Experience with our resident artist, Shelly Levy.

facts.text: The hotel overlooks verdant, private residential gardens.
facts.excerpt: we offer a boutique retreat in an atmosphere of Victorian elegance, overlooking verdant, private residential gardens

facts.text: The Victoria & Albert Museum, Natural History Museum, Science Museum, Royal Albert Hall and Kensington Palace and Gardens in Hyde Park are a short walk from the hotel.
facts.excerpt: A short walk from the hotel are world-renowned attractions such as the Victoria & Albert Museum, Natural History Museum, Science Museum and the Royal Albert Hall, alongside Kensington Palace and Gardens in Hyde Park.

facts.text: The hotel holds a Forbes Five-Star rating.
facts.excerpt: Our commitment to excellence has earned us the prestigious Forbes Five-Star rating

facts.text: The hotel uses locally sourced produce, manages food waste and has eliminated single-use plastics.
facts.excerpt: we use locally sourced produce for our menus, conduct food waste management procedures, and have eliminated single-use plastics

facts.text: The hotel occupies numbers 17 and 19 Egerton Terrace, which were in use as a private hotel by the late 1890s.
facts.excerpt: By the late 1890s, numbers 17 and 19 had passed into use as a private hotel.

facts.text: The hotel is part of the family-owned Red Carnation Hotel Collection.
facts.excerpt: reflecting the warmth and inclusivity of the family-owned Red Carnation Hotel Collection

facts.text: Studio suites have plush decor, refined artwork and bespoke amenities.
facts.excerpt: Our studio suites exude timeless elegance with their plush decor and luxurious furnishings. Featuring refined artwork and bespoke amenities

facts.text: The Dining Room hosts private afternoon teas and dinners for up to 15 guests.
facts.excerpt: catering for drinks and canapé receptions for up to 20 people and private afternoon teas and dinners for up to 15 guests

facts.text: The breakfast was recently voted the UK's best.
facts.excerpt: in our Dining Room, indulge in our exceptional breakfast, recently voted the UK's best

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler describes the building as Georgian with art by Picasso and Matisse.
facts.excerpt: Rooms at the Georgian Egerton House Hotel are decked out with artwork by Picasso, Toulouse-Lautrec, and Matisse.

contradictions.note: Official p5 says Victorian townhouse dating from 1843; Conde Nast Traveler p10 calls it Georgian
